text:
Drew Doughty plays his 1,300th NHL game tonight in Montreal, every one of them for the Kings, two Stanley Cups and a Norris along the way. The off-ice story is his contract: he has hired agent Pat Brisson, per The Hockey News, and Pro Hockey Rumors reports he wants to finish his career in Los Angeles. The Athletic's Sean McIndoe put him on a list of veteran stars whose playoff careers may already be over, which is the uncomfortable backdrop.

On the ice, he is a defense-first player now. Evolving-Hockey had most of his value last season from even-strength defense, 88th percentile at taking chances away, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking credits his entry denials and clean exits. This season, though, Los Angeles takes 46% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on (expected goals measure the quality of chances), almost six points worse than without him. Eight points in 20 games is about his range. He is 36; the job now is minutes, not miracles.
